scope: Individual source/native/orbit/street observations only. Scores4/5 are provisional structural screening, never aesthetic approval or live runtime coverage. All six acceptance gates remain false.

temperate.defect: The fuller toe now follows the long source bank, but exposed pale soil is too broad and the grass crest still lacks the original broken dark/pale patches.
The long rising bank retains too little visible grass and too much pale toe in the registered view; the far-end cap and sediment scallops are not source-faithful.
The near-facing grass band is too thin against a repeated pale shelf; the source's larger mottled green shoulder and light rim are not reproduced.
The length and broad green/pale placement are recognizable, but the crest is too regularly stepped and its pale lower edge is overexposed.
Both corner arms are now present, but the soil-filled concavity dominates the source's mostly grass return and the middle cap silhouette remains angular.
The V-shaped owner now has both arms, but its native grass centre is thinner than the original bowl and the long pale edge is too uniform.
The left-return corner has the correct broad arrangement, but original upper-tip soil placement and the green concave cap/notches are simplified.
The rear arch reads coherently as a shallow bank, but its pale base is too broad and the source's irregular green peak and inner rim are flattened.
The inner return is larger than the rejected first wedge but remains a stepped arm pair instead of the source's compact pale/green rounded nub.
The native inner owner still appears as a narrow pale V rather than the source's fuller rounded green-centred patch; the upper pale shoulder is uneven.
The small inner cap is too angular and soil-heavy; its left green spur and pale near-side lump do not match the original compact contour.
The pale-front/green-back arrangement is recognizable, but the native crest is taller and the three-course street profile remains too regular.

arctic.defect: The actual ordinary Arctic source is brown/green and the candidate now has sediment relief, but it still exposes too much light soil and too little mottled turf.
The ordinary Arctic long bank is too pale in the native view; the original brown/olive shoulder, far end and bright rim remain underfilled.
The near-facing brown/olive crest is too narrow, with repeated wide pale sediment strips and insufficient source green flecks.
The native lower pale/upper brown relationship is readable, but the source's irregular olive/brown transitions and return-tip shape remain approximate.
The ordinary Arctic corner now retains both arms, but pale sediment dominates the narrow return and the source's brown/olive central patch is not matched.
The actual snowy owner now has independent snow paint, but the V remains too shallow and smooth, missing the source's cyan/gray mottling and unequal snowy endpoints.
Snow colour ownership is repaired, but the surviving soil tip appears on the lower return rather than the original upper tip; the snow notches and cap shading are still inaccurate.
The ordinary brown/pale rear arch is coherent, but the cap peak is too triangular and its exposed sediment band is too wide and regular.
The ordinary inner patch is angular and pale-heavy instead of the source's round brown/olive/pale nub; the tiny spur and cap-edge paint remain unresolved.
The ordinary Arctic inner native view underfills the rounded brown cap and overstates a pale V-shaped toe; its tiny side shades are not source-faithful.
The original compact pale/olive inner lump becomes a two-arm stepped patch with an overly broad exposed soil return.
The ordinary Arctic pale-front/brown-back arrangement is recognizable, but the crest height and light/dark side distribution remain too regular.

tropic.defect: The muted green source bank is recognizable, but the candidate's light sediment toe is too broad and its repeating stepped crest misses the original turf mottling.
The original broad muted-green shoulder is too thin in the registered rising bank; pale soil strips dominate and the far cap lacks source detail.
The native tropical bank overstates pale sediment and underfills the broad muted-green near shoulder; its repeating cuts are not the source edge.
The green/pale relationship is plausible, but the lower light edge is too broad and the native crest/notches remain simplified.
The broad muted-green corner retains both arms, but the central pale concavity and angular middle spur differ from the original thin turf return.
The tropical bowl is too pale and shallow in the native view, with a narrowed green centre and overly regular arm ends.
The return arrangement is readable, but its upper-tip source pale paint and the green cap's taper/notch profile remain inaccurate.
The rear green/pale arch is recognizable, but the green peak is too sharp and the broad pale base overwhelms the original narrow margin.
The inner muted-green/pale source nub is replaced by a longer angular return with too much exposed light soil.
The compact green inner cap is still underfilled and V-shaped; the original pale upper shoulder and rounded lower patch are not retained.
The source's small green-left/pale-right lump remains an angular stepped two-arm patch with simplified paint and contour.
The pale-front/green-back order is readable, but the native crest height and regular street-course paint still do not match the source.

The yellow/pale source shoulder is underfilled while the exposed sediment strips dominate; the pale/ochre transition remains too angular.
The yellow/pale order is readable, but both pale endpoints and the narrow near rim still have incorrect contours and overly regular face paint.
The yellow arms and pale middle cap are retained, but the pale cap contour and earth-filled concavity differ from the original compact painted return.
The yellow middle and separately pale endpoints are repaired, but the V-shaped soil margin is still too broad and the pale end shapes remain simplified.
The pale-middle/yellow-arm return is recognizable, but the upper tip, central cap width and pale side shading remain inaccurate.
The yellow rear middle and pale ends are repaired, but the peak and inner pale rim remain too angular and earth-heavy.
The source's compact pale/earth inner nub is too angular, with a larger pale cap and an invented-looking yellow spur that remains unapproved.
The yellow middle is retained rather than the rejected pale-centre inversion, but the native cap is still too narrow and the pale shoulder differs from the original rounded patch.
The tiny pale/earth inner lump has become a stepped arm pair with too broad a cap and simplified side shades.
